findings.F1: The idea's own forecast predicts the next day on the predicted side, with a pooled slope t of 4.24 over 17,380 bars and a raw-z slope t of 4.74. The test is inconclusive because the timing gain is measured on the book after fees: before fees the position earned 0.000573 a day, but fees took 0.000725 a day at a turnover of 0.66 per bar, leaving -0.000157 a day.
findings.F2: The reversal holds after falls only. Next-day excess return rises with the size of the fall (slope t 3.90, n 8,514 by forecast; t 3.61, n 7,151 by the raw z). After rises, the slope on the forecast is the wrong way (t -2.02, n 8,866), so larger rises are followed by slightly larger rises, not falls.
findings.F3: In the book, the long side after falls carries the timing gain, at 0.001095 a day against 0.000122 on the short side after rises. The top forecast deciles 8 and 9, the largest falls, have next-day excess returns of +0.0037 (t 3.14) and +0.0047 (t 3.60).
findings.F4: The rebound after falls is a one-day effect. Its slope t drops from 3.61 at 1 day to 1.12 at 3 days (n 2,245) and 0.65 at 5 days (n 1,476). It is stronger when the coin is below its 50-day average (t 2.68, n 2,888) than above it (t 1.45, n 2,197).
findings.F5: After rises, the move continues over longer horizons. The slope of the 5-day excess return on minus z within rises is -0.0109 (t -2.51, n 1,365), and -0.0044 at 3 days (t -1.98, n 2,466): the larger the one-day rise relative to the usual move, the larger the further rise over 5 days.
findings.F6: The effect is uneven across coins and years. It is strong in XMR (t 4.84) and LTC (t 2.26), and absent in BTC (t 0.99), XRP (t 0.89) and ZEC (t -0.04). It is strong in 2018 (t 3.13) and 2020 (t 3.27) and fades in 2024 (t 0.01) and 2025 (t -1.10).

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall relative to the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 20 days, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a coin after an unusually large one-day fall, in proportion to the fall, and hold it for one day, rather than sell into the fall.
ideas.name: one-day fall rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day rise relative to the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 20 days, the larger its further rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would keep or add to a long after an unusually large one-day rise rather than fade it.
ideas.name: large rise continues five days
